# ankra_cluster_security_policy_mode (Resource)

The mode of a cluster's security baseline (`ankra security policy-mode`): `audit` observes and reports, `enforce` blocks non-compliant admissions, and `off` uninstalls the Kyverno policy engine and leaves native pod security observing. Switching back to `audit` or `enforce` does not reinstall Kyverno. The change goes through the cluster's stack update and, when the cluster has a GitOps repository, is committed there. The cluster must carry the security baseline; one without it answers 404.

`mode` reads back as the mode last asked for, so a change made with the CLI or the portal shows as drift; `policy_mode` is what the cluster stores now. Destroy leaves the mode as it is.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ankra_cluster_security_policy_mode" "prod" {
  cluster_id = "0b6f1d2e-1111-4222-8333-944445555666"
  mode       = "enforce"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Identifier of the cluster. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `mode` (String) `audit`, `enforce` or `off`.

### Read-Only

- `commit_sha` (String) The GitOps commit that carried the last change made by this resource; null when the cluster has no GitOps repository.
- `id` (String) The cluster id.
- `policy_engine_installed` (Boolean) Whether a Kyverno or kyverno-policies add-on is installed on the cluster.
- `policy_mode` (String) The mode the cluster stores now: `enforce`, `audit`, or `off` when no policy engine is installed (also after `audit` was asked for on a cluster whose engine was retired).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imported by cluster id.
terraform import ankra_cluster_security_policy_mode.prod 0b6f1d2e-1111-4222-8333-944445555666
```
